name: OMTech Polar 2 70W
tagline: Desktop CO₂ with a 28 × 14 in bed, 70W glass tube and built-in water cooling
tldr: The Polar 2 70W replaces the original Polar with a much larger 710 × 360 mm bed, a 70W glass CO₂ tube cooled by an internal 4.3 L water loop, a 16 MP full-bed camera, one-touch auto-focus and a rotary in the box. It is the cutting-first, lower-cost half of the Polar 2 line; the 50W RF version engraves faster and finer. No independent long-term review yet.
mainObjective: Desktop CO₂ cutting of acrylic and wood on a bigger bed, without an external chiller

priceRange.note: OMTech store price (Oct 2026), list $5,199.99; package includes rotary, LightBurn key and exhaust kit

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm acrylic

cut: Clear and coloured acrylic up to ~10 mm (estimate)
cannot: Sheets longer than the bed (no pass-through)

pros: 710 × 360 mm bed: about 60% more area than the original Polar, on a desk
Internal 4.3 L closed water loop: no separate chiller or bucket to plumb
Complete package: 16 MP full-bed camera, auto-focus, air assist, exhaust fan, rotary and LightBurn key
Most raw cutting wattage for the money in the Polar 2 line
cons: Glass tube rated around 10,000 hours versus 30,000 for the RF version: plan a replacement
No pass-through, so long sheets must be cut down first
Brand-new model: no independent long-term review yet, specs are OMTech's
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 70W glass-tube SKU of the Polar 2. Compare it with the 50W RF: choose the 70W if cutting acrylic and wood is most of your work and budget matters. Both share the same chassis, camera and software.
proTips: Check the coolant level and temperature before long cutting runs, even with the internal loop. Use the camera for job placement but verify alignment with a test mark. Duct the exhaust outside: the built-in fan moves smoke, it does not filter it.

faq.question: 70W glass or 50W RF: which Polar 2 should I choose?
faq.answer: The 70W glass tube cuts thicker material for $1,300 less. The 50W RF tube engraves faster (up to 2,000 mm/s), with a finer spot and a tube rated for about three times longer, and needs no water loop. Cutting-first shops lean 70W; photo and detail engraving lean RF.

faq.question: Does the Polar 2 70W need a water chiller?
faq.answer: Not a separate one: OMTech lists an internal 4.3 L closed-loop water cooling system. You still need to keep the coolant topped up and the room temperature reasonable.

faq.question: Is the Polar 2 a replacement for the original Polar?
faq.answer: Yes. The original Polar 50W (400 × 300 mm) is no longer sold new by OMTech; the Polar 2 keeps the desktop format with a 710 × 360 mm bed.

editorialDepth.advantages: The Polar 2 70W fixes the original Polar's main limit, its small bed, while keeping a desktop footprint. With the water loop built in and camera, auto-focus, rotary and LightBurn included, it is close to a turnkey CO₂ for acrylic signage, wooden boxes and small production runs.
editorialDepth.limitations: A glass tube wears out faster than an RF source and is slower on fine engraving. There is no pass-through, the machine is large for a desk (about 1.2 m wide), and smoke must be vented outside. Specs are manufacturer figures until independent reviews arrive.
